name: The five causes of action (BhG 18.13–15)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Every action undertaken with body, speech and mind, right or wrong, has five causes declared in the Sāṃkhya: the seat (adhiṣṭhāna), the doer (kartṛ), the various instruments (karaṇa), the manifold distinct activities (ceṣṭā) and the divine (daiva) as fifth; hence one who sees the self alone as the doer does not see, and one whose state is not ego-made is not bound (18.13–17).

name: The threefold impulse and threefold composition of action (karma-codanā, karma-saṃgraha)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Knowledge, the object of knowledge and the knower are the threefold impulse to action; instrument, act and doer the threefold composition of action (18.18); knowledge, action and doer are then each classified by the guṇas (18.19–28).

name: Oṃ tat sat, the threefold designation of brahman

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: '(Oṃ) tat sat' is the threefold designation of brahman by which the brāhmaṇas, Vedas and sacrifices were ordained; the expounders of brahman begin rites with oṃ; seekers of release perform them with 'tat' without aiming at fruit; 'sat' names being, goodness, praiseworthy acts, steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and giving and action for that purpose; what is done without faith is 'asat' (17.23–28).

name: Scripture as the authority for what is to be done (śāstraṃ pramāṇam)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Scripture is the authority for settling what is to be done and not done; whoever sets aside its ordinance and acts from desire attains neither perfection, happiness nor the highest goal; knowing its ordinance one should act (16.23–24). Austerity not enjoined by scripture, done with hypocrisy and tormenting the body, is of demonic resolve (17.5–6). Arjuna's question about those who set the ordinance aside but sacrifice with faith (17.1) opens the teaching on threefold faith.

name: The three kinds of sacrifice (yajña)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Sacrifice is sāttvic when offered as seen in the rule by those who do not desire fruit, with the mind settled on 'it ought to be offered'; rājasic when aimed at fruit or for show; tāmasic when without rule, distribution of food, mantras, fee and faith (17.11–13).

name: The divine and demonic endowments (daivī and āsurī sampad)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Two creations of beings, divine and demonic (16.6): the divine endowment of twenty-six qualities (16.1–3) leads to release, the demonic (hypocrisy, arrogance, excessive pride, anger, harshness, ignorance, 16.4) to bondage (16.5). The demonic know neither engaging nor refraining, say the world is without truth, foundation or Lord and caused by desire, live in insatiable desire and anxiety, boast, sacrifice in name only, hate the Lord in all bodies, and are cast into demonic wombs birth after birth, to the lowest state (16.7–20).

name: The three kinds of faith (śraddhā)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Faith is threefold, born of one's nature; each one's faith accords with his being, and the person is made of faith — as his faith, so is he; the sāttvic worship gods, the rājasic yakṣas and rākṣasas, the tāmasic the departed and spirits (17.2–4).

name: The three kinds of food (āhāra)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Food dear to each is threefold: sāttvic (increasing life, vitality, strength, health, happiness and delight; savoury, rich, lasting, heart-pleasing), rājasic (pungent, sour, salty, very hot, sharp, dry, burning; bringing pain, grief and disease), tāmasic (spoiled, tasteless, putrid, stale, leftover, impure) (17.7–10).

name: The three kinds of giving (dāna)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Giving is sāttvic when given as what ought to be given, to one who makes no return, at the right place and time and to a fit recipient; rājasic when for a return or a fruit or given grudgingly; tāmasic when at the wrong place and time, to the unfit, without respect and with contempt (17.20–22).

name: The threefold austerity (tapas) of body, speech and mind

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Austerity of body, speech and mind (17.14–16), each sāttvic when practised with highest faith by the yoked who do not desire fruit, rājasic when for respect and show (unstable), tāmasic when from a deluded notion, self-tormenting or aimed at another's ruin (17.17–19).

name: Relinquishment and renunciation (tyāga and saṃnyāsa)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Asked the truth of saṃnyāsa and tyāga (18.1), Kṛṣṇa reports that sages call saṃnyāsa the laying aside of desire-prompted acts and the discerning call tyāga the giving up of the fruit of all acts (18.2), reports two views on giving up action (18.3), and concludes that sacrifice, giving and austerity are to be done without attachment and fruit (18.4–6); relinquishment is tāmasic, rājasic or sāttvic (18.7–9); the relinquisher is the one who gives up the fruit, since the embodied cannot give up action entirely (18.10–12); renunciation brings the perfection of naiṣkarmya (18.49); all actions are to be renounced to Kṛṣṇa in thought (18.57).

name: The guṇa-classification of knowledge, action, agent, intellect, steadfastness and happiness

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: After the threefold impulse and composition of action (18.18), knowledge (18.20–22), action (18.23–25), doer (18.26–28), understanding (18.30–32), steadfastness (18.33–35) and happiness (18.36–39) are each classified as sāttvic, rājasic and tāmasic, grounded in the statement that no being on earth or among the gods is free of the three guṇas (18.40).

name: The varṇas by guṇa and action

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: The actions of brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas and śūdras are distributed by the guṇas arising from their own nature (18.41), with each class's actions listed (18.42–44); one attains perfection devoted to one's own action (18.45–46).

name: One's own dharma (svadharma)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: One's own dharma is better, though deficient, than another's well performed; doing action fixed by one's own nature one incurs no fault (18.47); the innate action is not to be abandoned even if faulty, for every undertaking is enveloped in fault as fire in smoke (18.48); worshipping with one's own action the one from whom beings proceed, one attains perfection (18.46).

name: Actionlessness (naiṣkarmya)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: The supreme perfection of freedom from action is attained through renunciation by one with unattached understanding, self-conquered and free of longing (18.49); it is the starting point for the account of how the perfected one attains brahman (18.50–53).

name: The self is not the agent; the guṇas act

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Since every action has five causes, one who sees the self alone as the doer, through unrefined understanding, does not see; one whose state is not ego-made and whose understanding is untainted does not slay and is not bound even in slaying (18.16–17).

name: The Lord in the heart of all beings

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: The Lord dwells in the region of the heart of all beings, making them revolve by his māyā as if mounted on a machine (18.61); the demonic hate the Lord in their own and others' bodies (16.18) and unscriptural austerity torments him within the body (17.6).

name: The Lord's grace (prasāda)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: By the Lord's grace one who does all actions while taking refuge in him attains the eternal abode (18.56); with thought on him Arjuna will cross all difficulties (18.58); by his grace comes supreme peace (18.62); Arjuna's memory is regained by it (18.73); Sañjaya heard by Vyāsa's grace (18.75).

name: Surrender to the Lord (śaraṇāgati / prapatti)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Go to the Lord in the heart alone for refuge with your whole being (18.62); relinquishing all dharmas, come to Kṛṣṇa alone for refuge — he will free you from all evils; do not grieve (18.66, called the most secret word, 18.64).

name: Teacher, transmission and secrecy in the Gītā and epic

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: The teaching is 'more secret than the secret', to be reflected on before acting (18.63); the most secret word is given because Arjuna is dear (18.64); it is not to be told to one without austerity or devotion, unwilling to listen, or cavilling (18.67); one who teaches it to devotees reaches Kṛṣṇa and none is dearer to him (18.68–69); studying it is worship by the sacrifice of knowledge (18.70); hearing it with faith brings the worlds of the meritorious (18.71); Kṛṣṇa checks whether delusion is gone (18.72); Sañjaya heard the yoga directly from Kṛṣṇa by Vyāsa's grace (18.75).

name: Hell (naraka)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: The deluded demonic fall into a foul hell (16.16); desire, anger and greed are its threefold gate (16.21).

name: The three guṇas

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: No being on earth or in heaven is free of the three guṇas born of prakṛti (18.40); faith, food, sacrifice, austerity, giving, relinquishment, knowledge, action, doer, understanding, steadfastness and happiness are classified by them (17.2–22; 18.4–39).

name: No embodied being can remain without action

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: An embodied being cannot give up actions entirely (18.11); Arjuna's nature will compel him, and bound by his nature-born action he will do even against his will what he does not wish (18.59–60); all undertakings are enveloped by fault (18.48).

name: The guṇas as the doers of action

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Arjuna's resolve not to fight is vain: his nature (prakṛti) will compel him; bound by his own nature-born action he will do it even unwillingly (18.59–60).

name: Fate and human effort (daiva and puruṣakāra)

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: The Gītā names the divine (daiva) as the fifth of five causes of every action, beside the seat, the doer, the instruments and the activities (18.14).

name: Rebirth

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: The Lord casts the hateful demonic into demonic wombs in the rounds of rebirth; deluded birth after birth they go to the lowest state (16.19–20).
